title: The Domain of the Soul
coreMove: Stillness holds when values, wounds, wants, and relationships stop fighting your judgment; repair one inner breach before asking calm to carry the day.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose kindness sounds calm but carries resentment
exampleSpecs.stakes: a peaceful tone can hide a refusal to serve the person in front of you
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lionel and Leontine let Dorothy Day's hospitality expose the gap between warm language and lived care.

exampleSpecs.audience: adults who mistake moral presence for a soothing style
exampleSpecs.stakes: copying the surface of calm can miss the honest care underneath it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Heath expects a 1968 PBS clip to soothe the room, then sees that Fred Rogers' honesty is what changes it.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers tempted to turn service into image management
exampleSpecs.stakes: public calm can become branding while the real commitment is cut
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Tariq and Sloane let a short chat expose the gap between Dorothy Day language and actual Catholic Worker service.

exampleSpecs.audience: caregivers whose calm routine breaks when a child interrupts it
exampleSpecs.stakes: a quiet ritual can fail unless the next act repairs the relationship
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Xavier stops a polished calm routine and restarts in the Fred Rogers manner: patient, truthful, and relational.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who need a small picture of inner order made physical
exampleSpecs.stakes: service becomes real in small repeated care, not private warmth
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Leontine's kitchen detail makes Dorothy Day's Catholic Worker commitments visible without a speech.

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders who copy a trusted style while violating its care
exampleSpecs.stakes: a borrowed calm style can cover the one act that broke trust
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Vincent locates the failed taping's decisive misstep: copying Fred Rogers' surface while rushing a child.
